translations.source_sense_description: Art und Weise, von der eine Sache betrachtet wird

glosses: A position from which something is perceived; outlook; standpoint.

examples.text: From the operator's point of view, there is a large blind spot on one side of the machine.
From an economist's point of view, business is all about money.

From another point of view, it was a place without a soul. The well-to-do had hearts of stone; the rich were brutally bumptious; the Press, the Municipality, all the public men, were ridiculously, vaingloriously self-satisfied.

It has been suggested that Prothean data recording is highly dependent on a certain point of view, what Carl Jung described as the collective unconscious. The 'cipher' needed to comprehend the images implanted in Shepard's mind is the cultural knowledge of a Prothean: the archetypes, biological instincts, and common experiences universal to the race.

glosses: An attitude, opinion, or set of beliefs.

examples.text: His point of view is that there is only one true religion.

glosses: The perspective from which a narrative is related.

examples.text: The storyline in the film “The Usual Suspects” is presented from the point of view of an unreliable narrator.
Therefore, there may be no overt indication of viewpoint, either because the speaker fails to mark his or her viewpoint, or because he or she takes a neutral point of view.

glosses: A figure formed by two rays which start from a common point (a plane angle) or by three planes that intersect (a solid angle).

examples.text: the angle between lines A and B

glosses: The measure of such a figure. In the case of a plane angle, this is the ratio (or proportional to the ratio) of the arc length to the radius of a section of a circle cut by the two rays, centered at their common point. In the case of a solid angle, this is the ratio of the surface area to the square of the radius of the section of a sphere.

examples.text: The angle between lines A and B is π/4 radians, or 45 degrees.

The single-imaging optic of the mammalian eye offers some distinct visual advantages. Such lenses can take in photons from a wide range of angles, increasing light sensitivity. They also have high spatial resolution, resolving incoming images in minute detail.

glosses: A corner where two walls intersect.

examples.text: an angle of a building

glosses: A change in direction.

examples.text: The horse took off at an angle.

glosses: A viewpoint; a way of looking at something.

examples.text: In his first book since the 2008 essay collection Natural Acts: A Sidelong View of Science and Nature, David Quammen looks at the natural world from yet another angle: the search for the next human pandemic, what epidemiologists call “the next big one.”

For example, if I was trying to repitch an idea to a producer who had already turned it down, I would say something like, "I remember you said you didn't like my idea because there was no women's angle. Well, here's a great one that both of us must have missed during our first conversation."

glosses: The focus of a news story.
Any of various hesperiid butterflies.
A storyline between two wrestlers, providing the background for and approach to a feud.
An ulterior motive; a scheme or means of benefiting from a situation, usually hidden, often immoral.

examples.text: His angle is that he gets a percentage, but mostly in trade.

glosses: A projecting or sharp corner; an angular fragment.

examples.text: though but an angle reached him of the stone

glosses: Any of the four cardinal points of an astrological chart: the Ascendant, the Midheaven, the Descendant and the Imum Coeli.
To place (something) at an angle.

examples.text: The roof is angled at 15 degrees.

glosses: To change direction rapidly.

examples.text: The five ball angled off the nine ball but failed to reach the pocket.

glosses: To present or argue something in a particular way or from a particular viewpoint.

examples.text: How do you want to angle this when we talk to the client?

glosses: To hamper (oneself or one's opponent) by leaving the cue ball in the jaws of a pocket such that the surround of the pocket (the \"angle\") blocks the path from cue ball to object ball.
A fishhook; tackle for catching fish, consisting of a line, hook, and bait, with or without a rod.

examples.text: Give me mine angle: we'll to the river there.
A fisher next his trembling angle bears.

glosses: To try to catch fish with a hook and line.
To attempt to subtly persuade someone to offer a desired thing.

examples.text: He must be angling for a pay rise.

glosses: Lieu d’où l’on regarde, site d’observation, panorama.

examples.text: Par une douce soirée du mois d’août, en 1821, deux personnes gravissaient les chemins pierreux […] et se dirigeaient vers les hauteurs pour y admirer sans doute les points de vue multipliés qu’on y découvre.
Prenant pour point de départ notre point de vue, c’est-à-dire la Terre où nous sommes, nous pouvons de là nous diriger vers les autres planètes de notre système […]

À la frontière de quatre départements (Haute-Saône, Territoire de Belfort, Vosges, Haut-Rhin), le ballon d’Alsace constitue également l’un des plus beaux points de vue de la région (sommet à 1 247 m).
Un ancien « point de vue » d’où on ne voyait plus rien depuis longtemps, envahi de crottes de lapins et de fragon piquant.

Mystère du point de vue. La perspective change totalement la perception du paysage. On croit que celui-ci s’offre tout naturellement si l’on ouvre bien les yeux. C’est faux. Ce que nous voyons, nous le composons et l’inventons pour une large part.

glosses: Manière de voir les choses, façon de considérer un problème, notamment dans les locutions « au point de vue » ou « à tout point de vue ».

examples.text: Vous allez défendre vos points de vue, mais acceptez aussi les critiques.

Toutes les personnes qui ont vu de près les chefs des trade-unions sont frappées de l’extrême différence qui existe entre la France et l’Angleterre à ce point de vue ; les chefs des trade-unions deviennent rapidement des gentlemen sans que personne y trouve à redire.
Au point de vue réparations, le renvideur, étant un métier plus délicat, demande plus de réparations.

J’aurais parfaitement compris que Paul Boncour montât à la tribune et démontrât à la Chambre et au pays que le projet du gouvernement ne tenait pas compte, du point de vue bourgeois même, des nécessités actuelles.

glosses: Opinion particulière, personnelle.

examples.text: À mesure, en effet, que les années s’écoulaient, l’ancien ministre de maréchal Mac-Mahon modifiait, révisait ses points de vue. Il en venait à juger équitablement les hommes qu’il avait combattus.
De son point de vue, Elias Gil avait été un putain d’enfoiré de merde.

Но, несмотря на всевозможные точки зрения, всякий согласится, что есть такие преступления, которые всегда и везде, по всевозможным законам, с начала мира считаются бесспорными преступлениями и будут считаться такими до тех пор, покамест человек останется человеком.
